skier: turnPeriod is the duration of ONE turn (edge change to edge change). Default 4.5 s gives 0.22 turns/s vs measured 2.97±0.43 s for long carving (martinez2019): turns ~50 % too long.
style 'short' (0.45×4.5 = 2.0 s/turn at 13 m/s) vs measured 1.04 s/turn; short turns are also run at long-turn speed.

Default apex lateral acceleration 0.54 g, lean 28°, quasi-static load peak 1.14 BW vs measured GRF peaks 1.6–2.05 BW (implying ~1.2–1.6 g, 50–57° inclination): turn loads and lean are ~half of reality. Concept scenarios (boom moguls case 0.34 g / 1.03 BW, demo 0.47 g) are even gentler.

Speed is constant within ±1 % (p05≈p95); mean settles ≈1–2.5 m/s ABOVE vTarget because the skid controller is proportional only (gain 1.2 s⁻¹). Default mean 13.2 m/s is consistent with recreational radar means (12.4–13.4 m/s) but there is no population spread (SD 4 m/s measured) and no p95 case (17–20 m/s, INFERENCE).
skierAt() has no trunk pitch/roll/yaw oscillation and no vertical snow excitation; lean is whole-body. Each concept adds its own (boom360: ±4° pitch at v/λ, rough 1.2 m/s² hip RMS 1–30 Hz).
trunkAndVibration: boom360 rough 1.2 m/s² (default) / 2.0 (mogul scenario) hip RMS is LOW against measured weighted RMS 9.4–11.1 m/s² at the sacrum (racers, sporri2017) and 9.7/12.9 m/s² at the boot (instructors carve/short, supej2018). Proposed recreational vertical trunk RMS ≈ 2.6–2.7 m/s² groomed, ≈4.3 icy, ≈3.7 moguls (INFERENCE: scaled down for speed, softer snow, single axis; still below the racer figures).
boom360 roughness shape (∝f² up to 6 Hz, 1–30 Hz) misses the measured 4–10 Hz spine-resonance peak and the 15–25 Hz chatter band; replace with the two-band shape in trunkModel.

boom360 mogul pitch ±4° at 1.8 Hz (>1 Hz rate RMS ≈32 °/s) and 0.5 g bumps: same order as the proposal (±6°, ≈2 Hz at 3.5 m spacing, >1 Hz pitch-rate RMS ≈52 °/s, 4.5 m/s² bumps), but the amplitude is unmeasured for both (GAP). Bump wavelength 5 m in boom360 vs ≈3.5 m measured course spacing.
wind: Realised Iu equals the requested intensity; σv/σu 0.8 and σw/σu 0.5 match standard ratios; PSD slope −1.56 vs −5/3 Kolmogorov: OK; Lu 30 m matches IEC Kaimal 28 m at z = 5 m.

Gust factor G3s: model 1.30 (Iu 0.15), 1.38 (0.2), 1.49 (0.25), 1.55 (0.3) → peak factor g ≈ 1.9–2.0 vs WMO in-land 1.66 at Iu 0.25 (g ≈ 2.6). Model underestimates gust peaks ~25 % at a given Iu (24-mode sum-of-sines, lowest mode 0.02 Hz).
For U < 2 m/s the model floors σ at Iu·2 m/s (Iu realised 0.30 at U = 1): acceptable for calm-with-puffs but label it.

No Taylor advection: a skier moving 12 m/s into a 5 m/s wind sees the same >1 Hz share (6.2 %) as a fixed point; frozen turbulence would raise it ~2.3× (INFERENCE). The spatial phase term 0.01·φ rad/m is frequency-independent.

expert_carve.targets: turn 2.97 s, speed 13.3–13.9 m/s (supej2018, klous2014), peak GRF 1.76–1.93 BW (nakazato2011, supej2018)

short_turns.targets: turn 1.04 s (martinez2019; the model multiplies turnPeriod by 0.45 for short), peak GRF 1.89–2.05 BW (supej2018, nakazato2011); speed 8–10 m/s is INFERENCE (no measured short-swing speed found)

moguls_recreational.targets: one turn per bump at ≈3.5 m spacing (fisMogul) → ~1 s/turn; speed 5–7 m/s INFERENCE; resulting bump rate v/λ ≈ 2 Hz

defaults.kinds: Lu, Iu flat snow from IEC/WMO formulas (standard + INFERENCE for snow z0); 0.2/0.3 for complex slopes INFERENCE (GAP: no steep-slope Iu retrieved); envelope 0–9 m/s is a design choice below lift holds

modelChanges: raise mode count (≥48, ratio ≈1.13, lowest 0.005 Hz) or add a peak-factor check so G3s ≈ 1 + 2.6·Iu
replace spatial phase with Taylor advection: phase k·(x·ê_U) with k = ω/U so moving platforms see Doppler-shifted gusts

measured.note: Gust factors are 3 s / 1 s moving-average maxima over T divided by the T-mean (WMO convention uses a 10-min mean). The model clamps U to ≥2 m/s for σ, so calm runs still get σ=I·2 m/s.

advection_check.taylor_expected_moving: for a -5/3 range the >1 Hz share should grow ~ (3.4)^(2/3)≈2.3× (inference, Taylor hypothesis)

insta360.note: boom360 equiW 5760 (5.7K) is conservative; 8K only at 30 fps

hoverairX1ProMax.note: follow speed < p95 recreational speed (17–20 m/s INFERENCE) and below carving 13–14 m/s at times

jitterRms_3degps.verdict: UNSUPPORTED (no published video shake watchability threshold found)
jitterRms_3degps.evidence: CIPA DC-X011 covers stills; NASA cybersickness onset for constant rotation ≈0.415 rad/s ≈ 24 °/s (nasaSickness, VR not video); smooth-pursuit ~40 °/s
jitterRms_3degps.recommendation: keep 3 °/s as ASSUMED design target, label it as such, report also 10 °/s as a secondary "degraded" line; schedule a viewer test. Note the proposed trunk model gives 6–12 °/s (groomed/icy) and ~52 °/s (moguls) >1 Hz trunk rate: a body mount must reject 70–95 % on groomed and ~95 % in moguls.

addedMass_1p5kg.verdict: supported as product target, not a tolerance limit
addedMass_1p5kg.evidence: 1.5 kg = 1.9 % BW (80 kg) vs carriage guidance 10–15 % BW (popular) and military 30 % BW (militaryLoad)

bodyForcePeak_40N.verdict: UNSUPPORTED (no wearer jerk/impulse tolerance source found)
bodyForcePeak_40N.evidence: context only: turn GRF fluctuates 1.2–2 BW ≈ 950–1600 N (nakazato2011); 40 N ≈ 3–5 % of that
bodyForcePeak_40N.recommendation: keep as ASSUMED; better to express as a fraction of BW and as an overturning moment about the CoM

keMax_14p9J.evidence: FAA §107.120 Cat 2 = 11 ft-lb (14.9 J) transferred from a rigid object; Cat 3 = 25 ft-lb (33.9 J); Cat 1 = 0.55 lb; ASTM F3389 Method A < 73 J; EASA C0 < 250 g (no J), C1 < 900 g or < 80 J
keMax_14p9J.recommendation: keep 14.9 J; note it is a transferred-energy limit so applying it to KE is conservative; 80 J kill line comes from fragment-injury data (sust80J) — label as regulatory class boundary, not injury threshold; also add Cat 1 mass check (≤250 g, no exposed rotors)
